base.label: Motor 1 axis
base.description: The axis motor 1 drives.
base.rangeSource: EN config_app.c:1087-1095 (set_ma refuses an axis index of 6 or more, E112)
base.whatGoesWrong: A motor mapped to the wrong axis moves the wrong part of the machine, and a jog or homing move drives that part into its end stop.

base.label: Motor 1 microsteps
base.description: Microstep setting of the motor 1 driver.
base.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1511-1530 (0 refused with 108, E158; from 450.02 any value other than 1, 2, 4, 8 is refused with a range error and nothing changes)
base.whatGoesWrong: The TinyG v8 drivers support only 1, 2, 4 and 8 microsteps. Older builds stored any other value anyway, so the scale no longer matched what the driver did; 450.02 refuses it.

base.label: Motor 1 power management
base.description: When motor 1 is energized.
base.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1535-1541 (st_set_pm refuses MOTOR_POWER_MODE_MAX_VALUE = 4 or more, stepper.h:266-272)
base.whatGoesWrong: Modes 0, 2 and 3 de-energize the motor when it is not moving: holding torque is lost, and an unbraked Z axis can fall under its own weight.

base.label: Motor 1 polarity
base.description: Direction of motor 1: 0 normal, 1 reversed.
base.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1654 [0=normal,1=reverse] (set_01)
base.whatGoesWrong: A reversed motor drives the axis the wrong way: homing runs away from its switch into the opposite end, and soft limits protect the wrong side.

base.label: Motor 1 step angle
base.description: Degrees per full step of motor 1 (1.8 for a 200-step motor).
base.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1481 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most one revolution
base.whatGoesWrong: A wrong step angle scales every move on the axes this motor drives: the machine travels further or less than commanded and can leave its envelope.

base.label: Motor 1 travel per revolution
base.description: Millimetres (or degrees, on a rotary axis) the axis moves per motor revolution: screw lead, or belt pitch × pulley teeth.
base.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1499 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most 1000 per revolution
base.whatGoesWrong: A wrong travel per revolution scales every move: a 5 mm lead entered as 8 makes every move 60% too long.

base.label: A axis mode
base.description: How the A axis takes part in motion.
base.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:2756-2770 (linear axes up to 2, rotary up to 3; canonical_machine.h:287-293)
base.whatGoesWrong: Disabled, the A axis ignores its words while jobs and the preview assume it moves. Inhibited, its position follows the program but its motor is held at step 0: the next move of ANY axis drives the motor there, so inhibiting A away from 0 moves it back to 0, and leaving inhibited mode away from 0 moves it out to its position. In radius mode every A word is read as a length and turned into degrees, so A turns 360 / (2π × radius) degrees per mm (about 57× at radius 1).

base.label: A maximum feed rate
base.description: Highest feed (G1, G2, G3) velocity on A.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine
base.whatGoesWrong: Too high, feed moves can stall the motors and lose position; too low, jobs run slower than programmed.

base.label: A junction deviation
base.description: How far the path may round a corner at speed on A (larger is faster).
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 and at most 5 (typical values are hundredths of a millimetre); 450.02 refuses below 0.00001 (EN canonical_machine.c:2881-2892)
base.whatGoesWrong: Too large, corners are taken too fast and the motors can lose steps.

base.label: A homing jerk
base.description: Jerk used when homing and when stopping at a switch on A, in millions.
base.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:2897 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most 100 000 (millions), so the firmware never applies its divide-by-a-million path for values above 1 000 000 (canonical_machine.c:2900-2902), which would change the meaning of the number
base.whatGoesWrong: Too low, the axis overruns its switch before it stops; too high, the motors lose steps while homing.

base.label: A maximum jerk
base.description: Jerk limit of A moves, in millions (5000 = 5 000 000 000 per minute³).
base.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:2897 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most 100 000 (millions), so the firmware never applies its divide-by-a-million path for values above 1 000 000 (canonical_machine.c:2900-2902), which would change the meaning of the number
base.whatGoesWrong: Too high, acceleration exceeds what the motors can deliver and they lose steps silently; a stop also takes longer to come to rest than the overrun bound assumes.

base.label: A latch backoff
base.description: How far A backs off the switch to release it while homing.
base.rangeSource: host: 0 to 1000; a negative latch backoff fails homing with 245 (EN error.h:361)
base.whatGoesWrong: Too short, the switch never releases and homing fails; too long, the axis moves further than expected after touching the switch.

base.label: A homing latch velocity
base.description: Velocity of the slow A move off the switch that sets the home position.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine (0 fails homing with 243, EN error.h:359)
base.whatGoesWrong: Too fast, the home position repeats poorly from one homing to the next.

base.label: A radius
base.description: Radius used to convert linear units to degrees when A is in radius mode.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 and at most 10 m
base.whatGoesWrong: In radius mode a wrong radius scales every A move.

base.label: A minimum switch mode
base.description: What the A minimum switch input does.
base.rangeSource: EN switch.c:365-378 (sw_set_sw refuses more than SW_MODE_MAX_VALUE = 4, switch.h:42-47)
base.whatGoesWrong: A limit switch set to off no longer stops the machine at the end of travel. A homing switch on the wrong end, or on both ends, makes homing fail or drive into the far end.

base.label: A homing search velocity
base.description: Velocity of the A homing search towards the switch.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine (0 fails homing with 242, EN error.h:358)
base.whatGoesWrong: Too fast, the axis hits the switch hard and overruns it before it can stop.

base.label: A maximum switch mode
base.description: What the A maximum switch input does.
base.rangeSource: EN switch.c:365-378 (sw_set_sw refuses more than SW_MODE_MAX_VALUE = 4, switch.h:42-47)
base.whatGoesWrong: A limit switch set to off no longer stops the machine at the end of travel. A homing switch on the wrong end, or on both ends, makes homing fail or drive into the far end.

base.label: A travel maximum
base.description: Highest A machine coordinate: the soft-limit and homing-search bound.
base.rangeSource: host: a finite position within ±100 m (or ±100 000°); across keys tn < tm, at least 0.01 apart, and a range the firmware soft-limit test sees as one (float32, not fp_EQ, both ends above DISABLE_SOFT_LIMIT; travel.ts)
base.whatGoesWrong: A travel range larger than the machine lets soft limits and preflight pass moves that crash into the frame; homing searches that far before it gives up.

base.label: A travel minimum
base.description: Lowest A machine coordinate: the soft-limit and homing-search bound.
base.rangeSource: host: a finite position within ±100 m (or ±100 000°); across keys tn < tm, at least 0.01 apart, and a range the firmware soft-limit test sees as one (float32, not fp_EQ, both ends above DISABLE_SOFT_LIMIT; travel.ts)
base.whatGoesWrong: A travel range larger than the machine lets soft limits and preflight pass moves that crash into the frame; homing searches that far before it gives up.

base.label: A maximum velocity
base.description: Velocity of A rapid (G0) moves.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine
base.whatGoesWrong: Too high, the motors stall and lose position without any error; every later move is offset by the lost steps.

base.label: A zero backoff
base.description: How far A moves off the switch after homing before it sets zero.
base.rangeSource: host: 0 to 1000; a negative latch backoff fails homing with 245 (EN error.h:361)
base.whatGoesWrong: Zero stays on the switch: a limit switch can then trip during the first move of a job.

base.label: Default distance mode
base.description: Distance mode at power-up and after a program end: 0 absolute (G90), 1 incremental (G91).
base.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:3102 [0=G90,1=G91] (set_01)
base.whatGoesWrong: A file that assumes absolute coordinates runs every move relative to the last one in G91.

base.label: Default units
base.description: Units mode at power-up and after a program end: 0 inches (G20), 1 millimetres (G21).
base.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:3099 [0=G20,1=G21] (set_01)
base.whatGoesWrong: A file without G20/G21 runs in the default units: a millimetre file read as inches moves 25.4 times too far.

base.label: Motor idle timeout
base.description: Seconds after motion stops before motors in power modes 2 and 3 are de-energized.
base.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1602-1607 and stepper.h:281-282 (the firmware clamps to this range; the host refuses instead of letting it clamp)
base.whatGoesWrong: A short timeout drops holding torque soon after each move: an unbraked Z axis can fall.

base.label: Optional stop (M1)
base.description: Whether M1 pauses the program. Session only: not saved, off after a reset.
base.rangeSource: EN config_app.c:668 (set_01); config_app.c:1120
base.whatGoesWrong: With optional stop off, an M1 placed for a tool check or a clamp move does not pause the job.

base.label: Probe input polarity
base.description: Whether the probe input is normally open (0) or normally closed (1), independent of the switch type.
base.rangeSource: EN switch.c:334-348 (more than 1 refused; refused while a cycle runs); config_app.c:1119
base.whatGoesWrong: With the wrong polarity the probe reads as triggered at once, or never: a probing move drives the tool into the work or the touch plate.

base.label: Soft limits
base.description: Refuse moves outside the travel range once the axes are homed.
base.rangeSource: host: 0 or 1 (set_ui8 does not check)
base.whatGoesWrong: With soft limits off, a G-code or jog error drives the machine past the end of travel.

base.label: Spindle direction polarity
base.description: Level of the spindle direction output for clockwise: 0 low, 1 high.
base.rangeSource: EN spindle.c:62-81 (more than 1 refused; refused while the spindle is on or the planner is busy); config_app.c:1118
base.whatGoesWrong: The spindle turns the opposite way to M3/M4: tools cut backwards, and threaded tool holders can loosen.

base.label: Spindle enable polarity
base.description: Level of the spindle enable output for ON: 0 active low, 1 active high (the factory default).
base.rangeSource: EN spindle.c:62-81 (more than 1 refused; refused while the spindle is on or the planner is busy); config_app.c:1117
base.whatGoesWrong: With the wrong polarity, "spindle off" drives the output to the level an active-low relay or VFD reads as ON: the spindle starts when the app shows it stopped (SAFETY H11).

base.label: Switch type
base.description: Whether every homing and limit switch is normally open (0) or normally closed (1).
base.rangeSource: EN switch.c:350-363 (set_01; E106); switch.h:50-51
base.whatGoesWrong: The wrong type makes every switch read as pressed or never pressed: limits trip at once, or never trip at all and the axis drives into its end.

base.label: X maximum jerk
base.description: Jerk limit of X moves, in millions (5000 = 5 000 000 000 per minute³).
base.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:2897 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most 100 000 (millions), so the firmware never applies its divide-by-a-million path for values above 1 000 000 (canonical_machine.c:2900-2902), which would change the meaning of the number
base.whatGoesWrong: Too high, acceleration exceeds what the motors can deliver and they lose steps silently; a stop also takes longer to come to rest than the overrun bound assumes.

base.label: X latch backoff
base.description: How far X backs off the switch to release it while homing.
base.rangeSource: host: 0 to 1000; a negative latch backoff fails homing with 245 (EN error.h:361)
base.whatGoesWrong: Too short, the switch never releases and homing fails; too long, the axis moves further than expected after touching the switch.

base.label: X homing latch velocity
base.description: Velocity of the slow X move off the switch that sets the home position.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine (0 fails homing with 243, EN error.h:359)
base.whatGoesWrong: Too fast, the home position repeats poorly from one homing to the next.

base.label: X minimum switch mode
base.description: What the X minimum switch input does.
base.rangeSource: EN switch.c:365-378 (sw_set_sw refuses more than SW_MODE_MAX_VALUE = 4, switch.h:42-47)
base.whatGoesWrong: A limit switch set to off no longer stops the machine at the end of travel. A homing switch on the wrong end, or on both ends, makes homing fail or drive into the far end.

base.label: X homing search velocity
base.description: Velocity of the X homing search towards the switch.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine (0 fails homing with 242, EN error.h:358)
base.whatGoesWrong: Too fast, the axis hits the switch hard and overruns it before it can stop.

base.label: X maximum switch mode
base.description: What the X maximum switch input does.
base.rangeSource: EN switch.c:365-378 (sw_set_sw refuses more than SW_MODE_MAX_VALUE = 4, switch.h:42-47)
base.whatGoesWrong: A limit switch set to off no longer stops the machine at the end of travel. A homing switch on the wrong end, or on both ends, makes homing fail or drive into the far end.

base.label: X travel maximum
base.description: Highest X machine coordinate: the soft-limit and homing-search bound.
base.rangeSource: host: a finite position within ±100 m (or ±100 000°); across keys tn < tm, at least 0.01 apart, and a range the firmware soft-limit test sees as one (float32, not fp_EQ, both ends above DISABLE_SOFT_LIMIT; travel.ts)
base.whatGoesWrong: A travel range larger than the machine lets soft limits and preflight pass moves that crash into the frame; homing searches that far before it gives up.

base.label: X travel minimum
base.description: Lowest X machine coordinate: the soft-limit and homing-search bound.
base.rangeSource: host: a finite position within ±100 m (or ±100 000°); across keys tn < tm, at least 0.01 apart, and a range the firmware soft-limit test sees as one (float32, not fp_EQ, both ends above DISABLE_SOFT_LIMIT; travel.ts)
base.whatGoesWrong: A travel range larger than the machine lets soft limits and preflight pass moves that crash into the frame; homing searches that far before it gives up.

base.label: X maximum velocity
base.description: Velocity of X rapid (G0) moves.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine
base.whatGoesWrong: Too high, the motors stall and lose position without any error; every later move is offset by the lost steps.

base.label: X zero backoff
base.description: How far X moves off the switch after homing before it sets zero.
base.rangeSource: host: 0 to 1000; a negative latch backoff fails homing with 245 (EN error.h:361)
base.whatGoesWrong: Zero stays on the switch: a limit switch can then trip during the first move of a job.

base.label: Y axis mode
base.description: How the Y axis takes part in motion.
base.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:2756-2770 (linear axes up to 2, rotary up to 3; canonical_machine.h:287-293)
base.whatGoesWrong: Disabled, the Y axis ignores its words while jobs and the preview assume it moves. Inhibited, its position follows the program but its motor is held at step 0: the next move of ANY axis drives the motor there, so inhibiting Y away from 0 moves it back to 0, and leaving inhibited mode away from 0 moves it out to its position.

base.label: Y maximum feed rate
base.description: Highest feed (G1, G2, G3) velocity on Y.
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine
base.whatGoesWrong: Too high, feed moves can stall the motors and lose position; too low, jobs run slower than programmed.

base.label: Y junction deviation
base.description: How far the path may round a corner at speed on Y (larger is faster).
base.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 and at most 5 (typical values are hundredths of a millimetre); 450.02 refuses below 0.00001 (EN canonical_machine.c:2881-2892)
base.whatGoesWrong: Too large, corners are taken too fast and the motors can lose steps.

base.label: Y homing jerk

base.whatGoesWrong: Too low, the axis overruns its switch before it stops; too high, the motors lose steps while homing.
